paper.title_en: Constraining neutrino masses with localized fast radio bursts: Current bounds and future prospects
paper.abstract_en: The dispersion-measure (DM)--redshift relation of fast radio bursts (FRBs) provides independent low-redshift cosmological information for neutrino-mass inference. In this work, we perform joint analyses with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, using 120 localized FRBs with reliable host-galaxy redshifts and larger mock samples, to investigate the effects of sample size and the dark-energy model on constraints on the sum of neutrino masses, $\sum m_ν$. In the $Λ$CDM+$\sum m_ν$ model, CMB+FRB gives $\sum m_ν<0.21\,\mathrm{eV}$, substantially relaxed relative to the current CMB+DESI result. With 1000 simulated events, CMB+FRB1(mock) gives an upper limit of $0.12\,\mathrm{eV}$, which decreases to $0.035\,\mathrm{eV}$ for CMB+FRB2(mock) with 10000 events. The latter is more stringent than the CMB+DESI limit, demonstrating the potential of large localized FRB samples to constrain neutrino mass. When the model is extended to $w_0w_a$CDM+$\sum m_ν$, both the observed and mock samples yield upper limits of approximately $0.3$--$0.4\,\mathrm{eV}$, indicating that the assumed dark-energy model remains a dominant factor in these constraints. As localized FRB samples grow and the modeling of the individual DM contributions becomes more accurate, FRBs may provide further independent low-redshift information for constraining neutrino mass.
